TASK ID: independent-set-to-clique

USER REQUEST:
Write a polynomial-time reduction from Independent Set to Clique. problems.py defines both problems: SOURCE is Independent Set and TARGET is Clique. The SOURCE and TARGET class docstrings give the exact instance formats, yes-conditions and edge cases.

PROBLEM DEFINITIONS (the SOURCE and TARGET docstrings from problems.py, complete as given here):

SOURCE = IndependentSet
Independent Set.

Instance: {"n": n, "edges": [[u, v], ...], "k": k}
  * Vertices are 0..n-1. Edges are undirected pairs [u, v] with u != v;
    [u, v] and [v, u] are the same edge and may not both appear.
  * k is any integer.

Yes iff the graph has an independent set of AT LEAST k vertices: k
vertices with no edge between any two of them.

Edge cases: k <= 0 is always yes. k > n is always no. With no edges,
every set of vertices is independent.

TARGET = Clique
Clique.

Instance: {"n": n, "edges": [[u, v], ...], "k": k}
  * Vertices are 0..n-1. Edges are undirected pairs [u, v] with u != v;
    [u, v] and [v, u] are the same edge and may not both appear.
  * k is any integer.

Yes iff the graph has a clique of AT LEAST k vertices: k vertices with an
edge between every two of them.

Edge cases: k <= 0 is always yes. k = 1 is yes whenever n >= 1. k > n is
always no.

INPUT FILES: ["problems.py"]
WORKING DIRECTORY: /tmp/reduction-dvm93kcx

It provides SOURCE and TARGET with is_yes(instance), validate(instance) and random_instance(rng, scale); search it (e.g. with grep) only if you need something specific.

    reduce(instance) -> instance

The answer to the returned instance must be yes exactly when the answer to the input instance is yes, and reduce must run in polynomial time. Do not call the brute-force solvers inside reduce.

You may read files such as problems.py, but do not run, execute or test any code. Write reduce.py, then submit.

cd /tmp/reduction-dvm93kcx && cat > reduce.py <<'EOF'
"""Polynomial-time reduction from Independent Set to Clique.

Given an Independent Set instance G = (V, E), construct its complement graph
G' = (V, all pairs {u, v} not in E).  A set S is independent in G iff S is a
clique in G'.  Therefore the same k works for both instances.
"""


def reduce(instance):
    """Return the complement graph as a Clique instance.

    The input and output both use the format:
        {"n": n, "edges": [[u, v], ...], "k": k}
    """
    n = instance["n"]
    k = instance["k"]

    # Normalize source edges so reversed duplicates and self-loops do not
    # affect the complement construction.
    source_edges = set()
    for edge in instance["edges"]:
        u, v = edge[0], edge[1]
        if u == v:
            continue
        if u > v:
            u, v = v, u
        source_edges.add((u, v))

    # The complement contains exactly the non-edges of the source graph.
    complement_edges = []
    for u in range(n):
        for v in range(u + 1, n):
            if (u, v) not in source_edges:
                complement_edges.append([u, v])

    return {"n": n, "edges": complement_edges, "k": k}
EOF
